title: Rename `owned` parameter in `find_child()` to `match_owner` to reduce semantic confusion
body:
### Tested versions

always present.

### System information

Godot v4.x

### Issue description

The `owned` parameter in `Node.find_child(name: String, recursive: bool = true, owned: bool = true)` is semantically ambiguous and regularly misunderstood by users.

**Problem 1 – Ambiguity of `owned = true`:**
Many users assume that `owned = true` means "the node is owned by the current scene file", or that it was added via `add_child()` in the current script. In reality, it means `node.owner == self`, which relates to Godot's internal ownership mechanism used mainly for scene saving and instancing.

**Problem 2 – Ambiguity of `owned = false`:**
Conversely, when `owned = false`, users might reasonably assume it means "only search for nodes *not* owned by `self`" (i.e., excluding `self`-owned nodes). However, in practice it means "search all children regardless of ownership", which is a much broader behavior than the name implies.

This dual ambiguity leads to frequent developer confusion, incorrect expectations, and hidden bugs.

### Steps to reproduce

I propose renaming the `owned` parameter to something more explicit, such as `match_owner`.

The default value can remain the same (`true`), but the new name will communicate that the function is filtering children based on whether `node.owner == self`.

This change would make the behavior more transparent and prevent common misunderstandings.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

None
